//: This is an example configuration file for Git Blame Sifter.
You can place a `.blamesifterrc.json` file in your project's root directory.
Configuration is loaded with the following precedence: CLI flags > Environment Variables > .blamesifterrc.json > Defaults.
--- Rule Configuration ---
These options define the rules for identifying 'trivial' commits.
A case-insensitive regex pattern to match against the commit summary (the first line of the commit message).
Commits with a matching summary will be considered trivial.
Example: Matches conventional commits like 'chore: format code' or 'style(lint): fix indentation'.
A list of author names or emails to always treat as trivial.
The check is case-insensitive. Useful for filtering out automated commits from bots.
Enables or disables the advanced diff-based triviality check.
When `true`, the tool will perform a line-by-line diff for a commit's changes.
If the changes are determined to be purely cosmetic (whitespace, blank lines), the commit is marked as trivial.
This is a powerful but potentially slower rule. Set to `false` to disable it.
--- File Matching ---
Control which files are included or excluded from analysis using glob patterns.
An array of glob patterns for files to include in the analysis.
If not specified, it defaults to all files.
An array of glob patterns for files to exclude from the analysis.
This is useful for ignoring generated files, build artifacts, or lockfiles.
--- Output & Behavior ---
Customize the output format and runtime behavior of the tool.
The output format for the sifted blame results.
Available options: 'standard' (human-readable, like git blame), 'json' (machine-readable), 'summary' (author contribution report).
Display a spinner/progress indicator during long-running operations like parsing and history walking.
Set to `false` to disable, which is useful in non-interactive or CI environments.
Enable interactive mode. The tool will pause and ask for confirmation before sifting a commit identified as trivial.
This allows for manual review and override of the rule engine's decisions.
--- Advanced Git Options ---
A string of additional arguments to pass directly to the underlying `git blame` command.
This allows for advanced git features, like using a `.git-blame-ignore-revs` file to skip specific commits.
Example: '--ignore-whitespace -w'
